nodes.objective: Anchor the authority chain in the registry: recompute envelope and intent digests from contents, control root minting, make revocation survive re-minting, resolve parents from the registry, scope-check every action, and close the is_no_broader_than field gaps.
nodes.rationale: A5's audit showed the chain is self-referential: digests are format-checked, roots are free to mint, revocation keys on the digest string, and intersect_envelopes trusts caller-supplied parents. TOKEN-1010 and GRANT-1020 consume the registry surface this node fixes, so it lands first. This node must not touch effects.py or grants.py; those belong to its dependents. CONTRACT REPAIR 2026-08-13 (orchestrator, measured before dispatch): sealing the envelope digest changes the digest->envelope mapping the registry keys on, so it necessarily re-seals every fixture that registers an envelope -- 2 production minting sites (cortex/repository/local_execution.py:211, mission_adapter.py:139, both registering placeholder digests) and 7 test modules. Enforcement is therefore specified at REGISTRY ADMISSION plus a minting helper, not in ConstraintEnvelope.__post_init__: construction-time rejection would break 13 construction sites across 11 files for no additional security, since the registry is the boundary A5-F3 names. The write scope is widened to exactly the re-sealing surface, and GATEWAY-1040 gains a dependency on this node because its fixtures are in that surface.

nodes.objective: Make delivery grants attributable and finite: issuance is registry-anchored so an owner-issued grant is distinguishable from an agent-issued one, and every grant carries and enforces its own expiry.
nodes.rationale: A5-F6: DeliveryGrant's digest is unkeyed, so a grant cannot prove who issued it -- self-issuance is undetectable.
